$comment: The only config file. Anything that two scripts need to agree on, and anything
iHiD might want to change without reading code, lives here. Secrets never go in
this file: keys live in .env, which is gitignored (see .env.example).
engine: DeepSeek translates every language. There is no per-language engine
setting and no second adapter.
`model` is set here and nowhere else: deepseek-flash at reasoning_effort low,
iHiD's decision (2026-09-18). Allowed efforts are low, high and max.
`concurrency` is how many calls run at once within one (locale, type) group,
after the group's first call has gone out on its own to warm the provider's
prefix cache. DeepSeek allows 2500 concurrent requests per account for
deepseek-flash, so 1000 sends every item of a track at once after the warm-up.
`attempts` is calls per item: a failed call or a rejected answer is retried,
then the item is left absent and reported.
`catalog_batch_units` is how many catalog units go into one JSON batch.
`max_text_tokens` is the largest English text (estimated at four characters
a token) sent in one call. A whole file has to come back in one answer, and
an answer that hits the provider's output limit is truncated but still paid
for. A file above this limit is reported as a failure without being sent.
Chunking is not built. deepseek-flash takes a 1M context and returns up to
384K output tokens, so 150000 leaves room for thinking; nothing in the corpus
is close to it.
i18n_repo: where translated output is written and whose checker is run.
EXERCISM_I18N_REPO overrides it.
github: the issue queue. `issue_authors` are the only authors a queue issue
may have, written as `gh` prints them. The source repos' workflows open issues
as the Exercism i18n GitHub App, which `gh` prints as `app/exercism-i18n`.
`iHiD` is there only while website, docs, blog and problem-specifications still
run the old queue, which opens issues with his token; remove it once they call
exercism/i18n's reusable workflows. `commit_author` is who the automated
commits to exercism/i18n main are by: the app's bot user.
`singletons`, plus every repo in `org` with the `track_topic` topic, is the
allowlist of repos an issue may name. `attention_label` marks an issue a
person has to fix before it can finish; the retry sweep skips it (its name is
also written in .github/workflows/retry-stale-issues.yml). `over_cap_label` is
added before it when a change is above the word cap, so exercism/i18n's
rerun-source-check.yml can tell the source PR the translation is waiting for
approval (its name is also written there).
issue_word_cap: an issue with more untranslated English than this many words
(per locale) waits for iHiD instead of running on its own.
